subtitle: On the wind-scoured roof of the world, a king signs away freedom to keep a kingdom alive.

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of a solitary king against vast snow peaks, a scroll in one hand and a sword lowered in the other
panels.action: Delegs Namgyal stands on a windswept ridge above Leh, robes whipping in the icy wind, one hand gripping a rolled treaty scroll and the other resting on a sheathed sword, dawn light washing the Himalaya behind him.

dialogue.text: In 1684, amid Tibetan armies and Mughal ambitions, King Delegs Namgyal of Ladakh chose a treaty that saved his kingdom by chaining it.

i18n.hi: १६८४ में, तिब्बती सेनाओं और मुग़ल लालच के बीच, लद्दाख के राजा देलेग्स नामग्याल ने ऐसी संधि चुनी, जिसने राज्य बचाया पर उसे बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of Leh valley with palace, monasteries and caravans below snow peaks
panels.action: From high above Leh, the Namgyal palace clings to its crag while long caravans of laden yaks crawl through the Indus valley, smoke rising from scattered villages under the stark Ladakhi mountains.

dialogue.text: Ladakh in the late 1600s was a thin strip of life between stone and sky, ruled by the Namgyals and kept alive by caravans from Kashmir and Lhasa.

i18n.hi: १६०० के आख़िरी सालों का लद्दाख पत्थर और आसमान के बीच ज़िंदगी की पतली पट्टी था, नामग्यालों का राज, जिसे कश्मीर और ल्हासा की क़ाफ़िले ज़िंदा रखते थे।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot in Leh palace audience hall, Delegs Namgyal on throne listening to monks and merchants
panels.action: Inside the Leh palace hall, Delegs Namgyal sits on a low throne, brow furrowed, as a Drukpa monk and a weathered merchant kneel before him, a map of western Tibet spread on the floor between them.

dialogue.text: To the east lay Tibet under the Gelugpa regent Desi Sangye Gyatso; to the west, Mughal Kashmir. Delegs Namgyal’s Ladakh followed the Drukpa Kagyu, and traded with both.

i18n.hi: पूरब में गेलुग्पा शासक देसी सांगे ग्यात्सो का तिब्बत था, पश्चिम में मुग़ल कश्मीर। देलेग्स नामग्याल का लद्दाख द्रुक्पा कग्यू मानता था और दोनों से व्यापार करता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of high plateau battlefield with Tibetan banners advancing toward Ladakhi fort
panels.action: On a high, barren plateau, disciplined Tibetan soldiers march in lines under yellow and blue banners, their ranks stretching toward a distant Ladakhi fort perched on a rocky spur.

dialogue.text: In 1679, the Gelugpa government in Lhasa sent armies westward, claiming old rights in Ngari and complaining of Ladakhi support to their Drukpa rivals.

i18n.hi: १६७९ में, ल्हासा की गेलुग्पा सरकार ने न्गारी पर पुराने हक़ का दावा कर सेनाएँ भेजीं और लद्दाख पर अपने द्रुक्पा प्रतिद्वंद्वियों की मदद का आरोप लगाया।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of Delegs Namgyal in armor on Leh ramparts, looking toward the east
panels.action: Clad in mail over his robes, Delegs Namgyal stands on the Leh palace ramparts, wind driving grit into his face as he peers toward the unseen passes where rumours say Tibetan forces have already crossed.

dialogue.text: The Ladakhi chronicle remembers Tibetan fury and western Tibetan lands slipping away. Modern historians see politics, sectarian rivalry and control of trade roads woven together.

i18n.hi: लद्दाखी इतिहास तिब्बती क्रोध और पश्चिमी तिब्बत हाथ से जाते याद करता है। आज के इतिहासकार सत्ता, संप्रदाय की टक्कर और व्यापारिक राहों की जंग को साथ बुना देखते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of ruined gompa overlooking a captured valley, soldiers from both sides visible
panels.action: On a cliff above a cold river, a small monastery lies blackened and abandoned, while mixed groups of armed men pick through a captured village in the valley below, smoke hanging low in the thin air.

dialogue.text: The La dvags rgyal rabs tells of battles, sieges and losses in western Tibet. The Tibetan sources stress restoring Gelugpa authority and securing their frontier.

i18n.hi: ‘ला द्वाग्स ग्याल रब्स’ पश्चिमी तिब्बत में लड़ाइयों, घेराबंदियों और हारों की कहानी कहता है। तिब्बती स्रोत गेलुग्पा सत्ता वापस लाने और अपनी सीमा मज़बूत करने पर ज़ोर देते हैं।

panels.shot: interior close-up of Delegs Namgyal by lamplight writing a letter, snow seen beyond a narrow window
panels.action: By the flicker of a butter-lamp in a cold stone chamber, Delegs Namgyal bends over a rough table, painstakingly dictating a letter while snowflakes drift past the narrow window slit behind him.

dialogue.text: As Tibetan forces pressed west, Delegs Namgyal looked not east but down-valley. He appealed to the Mughal governor of Kashmir for help.

i18n.hi: जब तिब्बती सेनाएँ पश्चिम धकेलती रहीं, देलेग्स नामग्याल ने पूरब नहीं, घाटी की तरफ़ नीचे देखा। उसने मदद के लिए कश्मीर के मुग़ल सूबेदार को पुकारा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Srinagar’s Mughal garden with officials reading a mountain-sealed letter
panels.action: In a Mughal garden in Srinagar, Kashmir, robed officials sit by a canal as a scribe breaks the seal of a letter stamped with a mountain emblem, while an officer listens with narrowed eyes.

dialogue.text: In Srinagar, the letter reached the Mughal administration. Kashmir’s rulers had long watched the Ladakh route, where shawls, tea, wool and pashm flowed.

i18n.hi: श्रीनगर में वह चिट्ठी मुग़ल दफ़्तर तक पहुँची। कश्मीर के शासक बरसों से उस लद्दाखी राह पर नज़र रखे हुए थे, जहाँ से शॉल, चाय, ऊन और पश्म बहती थी।

panels.shot: heroic wide shot of Mughal troops marching into a mountain pass with artillery and standards
panels.action: Lines of Mughal soldiers in quilted armour and turbans wind through a high, narrow pass, small cannon dragged by teams of men and mules, green standards snapping in the harsh wind.

dialogue.text: Fidai Khan, the Mughal governor of Kashmir, sent troops upward. Their aim was not devotion, but influence, revenue and control of the high road.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर के मुग़ल सूबेदार फ़िदाई ख़ाँ ने फ़ौजें ऊपर की ओर भेजीं। उनका लक्ष्य भक्ति नहीं, असर, आमदनी और ऊँची सड़क पर क़ब्ज़ा था।

panels.shot: tense mid-wide of Tibetan and Mughal camps on opposite hills above a Ladakhi village
panels.action: Facing hills above a Ladakhi village hold two camps: one lined with Tibetan tents and prayer flags, the other with Mughal pavilions and cannon, while villagers move quietly between them under watchful eyes.

dialogue.text: By 1683, Tibetan sources acknowledge Mughal pressure from the west. Tibetan advance stalled, Ladakh became the field between two great neighbours, and negotiation crept in beside war.

i18n.hi: १६८३ तक तिब्बती लिखतें मानती हैं कि पश्चिम से मुग़ल दबाव आ लगा। तिब्बती बढ़त रुक गई, लद्दाख दो महा पड़ोसियों के बीच मैदान बन गया, और जंग के साथ-साथ बातचीत भी घुस आई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Temisgam fortress on a rocky hill, banners of all three powers visible
panels.action: The fortress of Temisgam crowns a rocky hill above the Indus, its walls crowded with Ladakhi guards as Tibetan, Ladakhi and Mughal banners flutter uneasily from different towers in the high wind.

dialogue.text: In 1684, at Temisgam, an agreement took shape. The Tibetan text of the treaty, studied later by scholars, sets out tribute, borders and trade in careful lines.

i18n.hi: १६८४ में, टेमिसगाम में एक समझौता जड़ पकड़ने लगा। बाद में पढ़ी गई तिब्बती संधि-पत्र में नापतौल कर नज़राना, सरहदें और व्यापार की शर्तें लिखीं हैं।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a treaty hall; Delegs Namgyal seated opposite Tibetan envoy, Mughal officer watching
panels.action: Inside a dim hall at Temisgam, Delegs Namgyal sits cross-legged opposite a Tibetan envoy robed in yellow, while a Mughal officer stands to one side, hands folded, observing every wordless exchange.

dialogue.text: The Ladakhi chronicle sees its king compelled by necessity; the Tibetan text records that Ladakh accepted Gelugpa authority in western Tibet and agreed to send yearly tribute to Lhasa.

i18n.hi: लद्दाखी इतिहास अपने राजा को मजबूरी में झुकता देखता है; तिब्बती दस्तावेज़ लिखता है कि लद्दाख ने पश्चिमी तिब्बत में गेलुग्पा सत्ता मानी और हर साल ल्हासा को नज़राना भेजने पर राज़ी हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on Delegs Namgyal’s hand pressing a seal onto the treaty scroll
panels.action: A close view shows Delegs Namgyal’s steady hand pressing a seal into warm wax at the base of a long, freshly written scroll, the grain of the wood and the rough fibre of the paper clearly visible.

dialogue.text: One clause fixed the frontier in western Tibet. Another regulated the caravan trade: Ladakhi merchants would carry specified tribute goods to Lhasa, under conditions set by the Gelugpa government.

i18n.hi: एक धार ने पश्चिमी तिब्बत की सीमा तय कर दी। दूसरी ने क़ाफ़िला-व्यापार बाँधा: तय नज़राना-सामान लद्दाखी सौदागर ल्हासा तक ले जाएँगे, शर्तें गेलुग्पा सरकार तय करेगी।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Delegs Namgyal listening as a Mughal officer quietly speaks to him aside
panels.action: In a corner of the hall, Delegs Namgyal leans slightly toward a bearded Mughal officer who gestures toward the valley below, his eyes intent, while the hum of treaty discussion continues behind them.

dialogue.text: Mughal power had its own price. The Ladakhi chronicle links their aid with concessions in Leh, including the building of a mosque and a recognised Muslim presence in the capital.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल मदद की भी अपनी क़ीमत थी। लद्दाखी इतिहास उनकी फ़ौजी सहायता को लेह में रियायतों से जोड़ता है—एक मस्जिद की तामीर और राजधानी में मुसलमान मौजूदगी की मान्यता।

panels.shot: wide shot of Leh town with palace, mosque dome and monastery all visible together
panels.action: Leh’s skyline shows the Namgyal palace above, a white monastery on one ridge and, near the bazaar, a modest mosque dome rising among flat-roofed houses, traders and townsfolk moving between all three.

dialogue.text: Archaeology and later accounts note the Leh mosque and Muslim communities as part of the new order. Ladakh remained Buddhist-ruled, but Mughal influence now stood inside its main town.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्व और बाद की लिखतें लेह की मस्जिद और मुस्लिम बस्तियों को नई व्यवस्था का हिस्सा मानती हैं। लद्दाख पर बौद्ध राज रहा, पर अब मुग़ल असर उसकी मुख्य बस्ती के भीतर खड़ा था।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of a caravan leaving Leh toward Tibet, with snow peaks and prayer flags
panels.action: A long caravan of yaks and men winds out of Leh toward the east, bales of wool and tea lashed tight, prayer flags snapping on a ridge as the trail climbs toward the high passes of western Tibet.

dialogue.text: After Temisgam, caravans resumed their slow crossings. The treaty’s trade clauses shaped how tribute and commerce moved between Ladakh and Lhasa for generations.

i18n.hi: टेमिसगाम के बाद क़ाफ़िलों की धीमी यात्राएँ फिर शुरू हुईं। संधि के व्यापार वाले हिस्सों ने पीढ़ियों तक तय किया कि नज़राना और सौदा लद्दाख और ल्हासा के बीच कैसे चलेगा।

panels.shot: interior archive-like shot of a later scholar studying the Temisgam treaty text by lamplight
panels.action: Centuries later, a scholar sits at a desk crowded with manuscripts, carefully tracing lines of Tibetan script on a fragile scroll under the warm glow of a modern lamp.

dialogue.text: Modern historians like Luciano Petech and John Bray have read and debated the Temisgam text, comparing Ladakhi and Tibetan memories and tracing its impact on later diplomacy.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार, लूसियानो पेतेक और जॉन ब्रे जैसे, टेमिसगाम के दस्तावेज़ को पढ़ते–तोड़ते रहे हैं, लद्दाखी और तिब्बती यादों की तुलना कर उसके बाद की कूटनीति पर असर खोजते हैं।

panels.shot: melancholic mid-shot of an older Delegs Namgyal overlooking the Indus from a terrace at dusk
panels.action: An older Delegs Namgyal stands alone on a palace terrace at dusk, gazing down at the dark ribbon of the Indus and the flickering lamps of Leh, hands resting on the stone parapet.

dialogue.text: A king can keep a throne and still lose his freedom.

i18n.hi: एक राजा तख़्त बचा सकता है, पर अपनी आज़ादी फिर भी हार सकता है।

panels.shot: wide, contemplative shot of the Himalaya at sunrise, Delegs Namgyal a small figure on a ridge
panels.action: At sunrise, the vast Himalaya blaze with light as Delegs Namgyal stands as a small silhouette on a distant ridge, the sky opening above him and the winding valleys disappearing into haze.

dialogue.text: The Temisgam Treaty shows how a small Himalayan kingdom survived between Tibet and the Mughals: by accepting tribute and limits, and proving that sometimes sovereignty is the art of choosing the least dangerous chain.

i18n.hi: टेमिसगाम की संधि दिखाती है कि छोटा हिमालयी राज्य तिब्बत और मुग़लों के बीच कैसे बचा रहा: नज़राना और सीमाएँ मानकर, और दिखाकर कि कभी-कभी सत्ता वही है जो सबसे कम ख़तरनाक ज़ंजीर चुन ले।

title_i18n.en: The Temisgam Treaty Saves a Kingdom
title_i18n.hi: टेमिसगाम की संधि–एक राज्य की बचत

subtitle_i18n.en: On the wind-scoured roof of the world, a king signs away freedom to keep a kingdom alive.
subtitle_i18n.hi: दुनिया की हवा-पिटी छत पर, एक राजा आज़ादी देकर अपना राज्य बचा रहा है।
